mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coincides with rising industrial production (INDPRO), creating a positive feedback loop that pushes S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the HOUST-INDPRO lead (p > 0.05 in 1000 permutations).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) below 6% over the next month are associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to risk-off sentiment in equity markets.
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE remains below 6% for > 40% of the month, 20-day forward returns are non-negative on average (mean > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate exceeds 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests supply-side weakness, which predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as market anticipates demand recovery.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in 70% of INDPRO < 105 instances (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail and industrial employment (PAYEMS and INDPRO) creates a dual-demand signal that drives positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than when either proxy moves alone (multivariate Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in jobless claims (PAYEMS) above 250K triggers a risk-off cascade that produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 250000 in a single reporting period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain non-negative in 80% of PAYEMS > 250K events (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: In inflationary regimes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero when CPIAUCSL > 2.5 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence (measured by a composite of available indicators) predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns as market anticipates economic recovery.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when GDPC1 is in continuous decline for > 30 trading days.
